items.title: 8.4 Dynamic equilibrium between two physical states

source_refs.note: Topic 8.4, printed pages 170-171, with Quick Check 8.2.

blocks.text: Dynamic equilibrium is a state in a reversible process where the rate of change in one direction is equal to the rate of change in the opposite direction. In other words, although there are continuous changes taking place, no net change in the system as a whole is observed. When a reversible phase change takes place for a substance, there is also a dynamic equilibrium between the two physical states. For example, at 0 °C, ice and water coexist in equilibrium. Water changes into ice whereas ice converts back into water at the same rate.
